title: Execution snapshot and timeline flows
summary: Visualize run opens a read-only text timeline for one request. It explains recorded activity overlap, waits, dependencies and outcomes. Viewing, resizing or copying the timeline does not.
html:
Execution snapshot and timeline flows

Visualize run opens a read-only text timeline for one request. It explains recorded activity overlap, waits, dependencies and outcomes. Viewing, resizing or copying the timeline does not admit an activity, reconcile a job or change run state. The Mermaid diagrams below explain that implementation; the product's copyable timeline itself is plain text.

execution_visualization.py assembles server evidence and registers the GET endpoint. run_execution_visualization.js contains the pure interval/text reducers and the browser disclosure lifecycle. The desktop shell mounts a view for each request, forwards deduplicated trace events and status changes, and disposes it when removing the task card.

See observability for trace retention and broader activity presentation, activity dependencies for admission, and top-level task dependencies for conversation task eligibility. These are separate authorities even when both dependency graphs appear in one visualization.

Evidence ownership

flowchart TD Native[Stored native activity state] --> Read[Read-only execution snapshot route] Trace[Retained request trace] --> Read Tasks[Conversation task store] --> Graph[Top-level task graph] Read --> Merge[Canonical records over event projections] Policy[Known-secret context and presentation policy] --> Project[Allowlisted labels and timing facts] Merge --> Project Project --> Revision[Content revision] Graph --> Revision Revision --> Snapshot[Execution snapshot JSON] Snapshot --> Analysis[Interval overlap and phase analysis] Snapshot --> Text[Plain-text timeline or summary] Analysis --> Text Text --> Panel[Request-owned browser disclosure] Panel --> Copy[Clipboard text]

The response contains activity identities, bounded labels and targets, states, batch/wave identities, dependencies, measured intervals, waits and recorded scheduler conflicts. It excludes raw argument/result objects. Labels still follow the selected redaction policy; an allowlisted schema is not a promise that every displayed value is confidential-data-free when redaction is disabled. The browser additionally removes control/directional characters and bounds labels by Unicode code points.

The route reads stored native state directly. A Controller-owned store uses its RAM view; the standalone compatibility store reads the native state JSON from SQLite. It bypasses the migration-capable load method. The retained trace is a separate read, and the optional task graph is another store read: the endpoint does not claim an atomic transaction across all three owners. Nor does it claim that input reads are limited to the fields in its final response.

Request and projection sequence

sequenceDiagram participant U as User participant V as Request visualization participant A as Execution snapshot endpoint participant N as Native store participant T as Trace store participant G as Task store U->>V: Open Visualize run V->>A: GET request execution-visualization A->>N: Resolve alias and read native state alt Missing or tombstoned run A-->>V: 404 V-->>U: Generic failure with Retry else Retained run A->>T: Read retained request trace T-->>A: Available events and timing A->>A: Merge records and project intervals and labels opt Request belongs to a conversation task A->>G: Read up to 500 tasks including archived G-->>A: Task states, edges and dependency evidence end A->>A: Hash projected content and task graph A-->>V: no-store snapshot with revision and observation time V->>V: Adopt changed revision and render literal text V-->>U: Timeline or bounded group summary end

The URL is /api/agent/native/{request_id}/execution-visualization. Route registration is owned by the native route group. Unknown/tombstoned runs return 404. Projection failures propagate as server errors; the browser presents a generic message and Retry without exposing the exception. Read errors do not trigger repair, resume, command execution or writes.

Projection precedence is explicit:

  1. Retained activity.* and scheduler.* events supply historical records and interval transitions. Recorded invocation presentations provide operation labels; recorded batch metrics supply conflict counts.
  2. Canonical activity batches and the foreground batch overwrite matching event fields. Dependency/background activity maps then overwrite matching fields for this run. Records for another run are excluded.
  3. Explicit not_admitted admission evidence corrects the displayed activity state. executed: false, rejected admission and blocked conflicts produce no execution interval. Neither a queued timestamp nor a job identity proves execution.
  4. Presentation helpers produce bounded labels and targets. Activities sort by measured start, otherwise creation time, then identity. Missing timestamps stay unknown rather than becoming zero.

The optional top-level graph lists up to 500 conversation tasks, including archived ones, ordered by creation sequence. It remains distinct from each activity's depends_on list. The route hashes this graph together with the activity revision so task-state changes can invalidate an otherwise settled run's visualization.

Timing and summary derivation

flowchart TD Events[Recorded start, wait, resume and terminal transitions] --> Intervals[Execution intervals and typed waits] Stored[Precise stored boundaries and retained capacity wait] --> Intervals Intervals --> Promotion[Split measured foreground and background intervals] Promotion --> Ends[Use finite increasing boundaries] Clock[Live snapshot observation time for explicitly open intervals] --> Ends Ends --> PerActivity[Merge each activity's spans for concurrency analysis] PerActivity --> Sweep[Sweep endpoints with ends before starts] Sweep --> Peak[Peak simultaneous activities] PerActivity --> Phases[Strictly overlapping execution phases] Ends --> Bars[Wait and execution text bars] Phases --> Group[Summary groups when more than 100 activities] Batch[Recorded batches and waves] --> Group Dependencies[Activity dependency layers] --> Group Peak --> Output[Timeline and explanatory details] Bars --> Output Group --> Output

ISO timestamps and finite numeric epoch seconds are accepted; booleans, invalid text and nonfinite values are unknown. Stored activity boundaries can refine trace emission times. Explicit dependency, capacity, approval, user and background launch waits are retained. A stored capacity-wait boundary provides a fallback when its event history is absent. Promotion splits an execution interval into foreground and background portions instead of treating the mere presence of a job ID as promotion.

Only an explicitly open interval on a live run extends to the snapshot's observed_at. Terminal and unresolved ends are never extended to today's clock. The text reducer ignores intervals with missing, reversed or equal boundaries. For peak concurrency it merges each activity's overlapping spans before counting, so resumed/overlapping records do not count the same activity twice. Touching intervals do not overlap: ends sort before starts, and phases join only across strict overlap. Waits contribute to the displayed time extent but not execution concurrency. The run-duration heading uses the run start and observed/terminal endpoint; it is not the sum of child durations. Individual detail durations sum the supplied valid activity spans, so they are distinct from the merged concurrency calculation.

The renderer clamps its layout to 70–120 columns. It paints waits with ., foreground execution with #, and background execution with =. Execution paint can cover wait cells at the chosen text resolution, and a measured very short activity receives at least one cell. Unknown timing uses [ ? ]; rejected or blocked activities without intervals have no invented running bar.

More than 100 activities default to a summary. Group selection prefers recorded batches/waves, then activity dependency layers, then measured overlap phases. Cycles or unresolved dependencies within the retained activity set remain an unresolved layer; absent external IDs do not create a synthetic layer. More than 20 groups become 19 explicit groups plus a remainder. Show all activities expands the recorded set locally. Recorded scheduler conflict counts appear only when supplied by the snapshot. An empty activity set states that no executable activities were recorded, while any top-level task graph can still be shown.

Refresh, caching and teardown

sequenceDiagram participant S as Shell or shared update broker participant V as Visualization disclosure participant A as Execution snapshot endpoint participant D as Mounted panel S->>V: Relevant trace, status or broker invalidation V->>V: Mark dirty and advance generation alt Disclosure collapsed Note over V,D: Keep dirty state without reading else Disclosure expanded V->>V: Coalesce behind one 350 ms delay V->>A: GET if no read is pending opt Another invalidation arrives during the read S->>V: Advance generation again end A-->>V: Snapshot or failure alt Successful response alt Changed content revision V->>V: Replace cached snapshot else Same content revision V->>V: Retain prior snapshot and observation clock end opt Still expanded and connected V->>D: Draw only if render key changed V->>V: Subscribe if live or task graph is present end else Read or rendering failure V->>V: Leave dirty and show Retry if open end opt Generation changed while request was pending V->>V: Schedule trailing read while expanded end end S->>V: Collapse or dispose V->>V: Clear timer, subscription and resize observer Note over V,A: An in-flight read may finish and cache evidence Note over V,D: Late completion does not draw or resubscribe while closed

The component fetches nothing at attachment. Opening a dirty, uncached or live view requests evidence; reopening a clean terminal view reuses its cache. Activity, batch, scheduler, graph, invocation and selected run/request lifecycle events invalidate it. Token deltas do not. The shell deduplicates trace events before forwarding them; the component does not assume cursor IDs increase across resumes. The shared broker listens to runs.changed and tasks.changed, filtering foreign request/run identities. Unscoped events and resynchronization requests also invalidate. A terminal run with top-level tasks keeps this subscription while expanded because its task graph can change.

Only one read is pending per view. An invalidation during that read requests a trailing pass; its response can be drawn before the trailing pass. The generation counter therefore preserves refresh demand rather than discarding every response started before a newer invalidation. Errors leave the view dirty for explicit Retry. The delay is event-driven; there is no periodic polling or browser clock that advances the timeline.

The server excludes observation time from its content hash. The browser replaces its snapshot only when that revision changes. Consequently, repeated equal-revision responses retain the earlier observed_at, even when the response carries a newer observation time. Live bars can remain frozen until execution/task evidence changes. This is the current cache behavior, not proof that execution stopped.

Rendered strings use run identity, content revision, accepted live observation time, measured width and summary mode as a key. The insertion-ordered cache holds at most six strings. An unchanged key preserves the existing <pre> node; resizing can reflow it without fetching. Copy writes the currently rendered text to the clipboard and reports success or a manual-selection fallback on failure.

Collapse stops scheduled reads, subscriptions and resize observation but retains cached evidence. Disposal also advances the generation and suppresses drawing; the shell removes the owned card/DOM. Neither operation aborts an already pending HTTP read or cancels the run. A scheduled callback finding a disconnected panel releases its observers without another read.

Verification evidence

The server fixtures cover alias resolution, tombstones, input immutability, interval boundaries, promotion, redaction and unchanged SQL state even when projection fails. Node fixtures cover overlap, touching intervals, bounded output, unknown timing and large summaries. Browser component fixtures cover on-demand reads, copying, generic retry, coalesced invalidations, collapsed responses, terminal caching, disposal and resize reuse. These use local synthetic evidence; they do not run a model or certify live Gateway behavior. Theme-specific cases are outside this documentation review.
